clue.text: Lively church breaking bread for service

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: bread is slang for money, and money given for service is pay
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A lively church service where communion bread is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread for service' reads as the communion wafer, but bread is slang for money, and money earned by service is wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacey describes something fast-moving and energetic, a close synonym for lively.

clue.text: Was controversial American writer given bad information, having promoted the Left?

indicators.note: in a down answer, promoting a letter means moving it higher, so the order changes

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
to be misled is to be given bad information

explanation.surface: A US author causes a stir after being misinformed and championing left-wing politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Left' sounds political, but it is just the letter L, lifted from near the end to sit third.
explanation.definitionFit: To polemise is to argue aggressively in a disputatious way, so having polemised is having been controversial.

clue.text: A little shrub, or a common climbing plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upward, so letters run backwards
only a small part of the words is taken, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters running across the end of shrub, or, a and the start of common

explanation.surface: Some modest shrub, or perhaps an ordinary creeper such as ivy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing plant' looks like one phrase meaning a creeper; climbing is the upward-reading signal and plant alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The carob is a Mediterranean evergreen tree whose pods are used as a chocolate substitute, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Blurring of my radar beam's outer part

indicators.note: a blurred image loses its sharp order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something smears the outer edge of my radar beam's signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radar beam' looks like one technical phrase; beam is in fact a ship's spar, the start of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is either end of a ship's yard, the horizontal spar holding a sail, so it is the extremity of a beam.

clue.text: Where the French cat almost opens hot salad

indicators.note: opens puts the shortened cat at the front of what follows
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a tabby is a striped cat
in French, 'where' is OU and 'the' is LE
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A question about where a French cat might be found opening something hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' applies to both words before it: OU (where) and LE (the). TABBY 'almost' loses its Y and 'opens' the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabbouleh is a Levantine dish of bulgur wheat, parsley and tomato served cold as a salad.

clue.text: Wanting a drink, son's ignored national speed limit

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so that letter disappears

parts.note: wanting a drink is being thirsty
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy is too thirsty to pay attention to the speed limit.
explanation.walkthrough: THIRSTY loses its S. In Britain, 30 mph is the standard limit on lit urban roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty miles per hour is the default British limit in built-up areas, a figure every UK driver knows.

clue.text: Giant insects biting husband

indicators.note: to bite is to close jaws around something, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: the first insect, a bee
H is the abbreviation for husband
the second insect, a moth

explanation.surface: Huge bugs chomping on a woman's husband, like a horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insects' supplies two of them, BEE and MOTH; the H goes into the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is a monstrous creature from the Book of Job, now any huge thing, so a synonym for giant.

clue.text: Dreamy Irish individual in charge captivates

indicators.note: captivates means holds captive, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: an individual is a single one

explanation.surface: A dreamy Irishman who is in charge charms everyone around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Individual in charge' is read as one piece, ONE plus IC, and it 'captivates' IR, holding it between the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneiric is a literary adjective meaning relating to dreams, so dreamy fits as a near synonym.

clue.text: Like aerobics? See weedy chap work

parts.note: lo means look or see
a wimp is a weedy, feeble man
to work is to act, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Watch a feeble man exercising: is this aerobics?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: some aerobics classes are low-impact.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-impact exercise spares the joints, and gentle aerobics routines are often sold under that label.

clue.text: Southern Indian city eradicates border plant

indicators.note: eradicates border means the outermost letters at each edge of the city are removed

parts.note: Chennai, formerly Madras, is a city in southern India

explanation.surface: A city in southern India wipes out a plant growing along a garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' suggests a garden bed, but here it means the edges of CHENNAI: losing C and I leaves the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a flowering shrub whose leaves give the reddish dye used on hair and skin.

clue.text: Broadcaster reluctant to cover opening of Rocky III in Berlin

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so one piece encloses the rest

parts.note: loth is a variant spelling of loath, unwilling

indicators.note: being in Berlin means using German, so the number is given in that language
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Rocky
drei is German for three

explanation.surface: A TV channel hesitates to show a German screening of Rocky III.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numeral is three, rendered in German. Lord Reith was the first Director-General of the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: John Reith founded the BBC's public-service ethos, so as its first head he is the archetypal British broadcaster.

clue.text: King drank with journalist at the front

indicators.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist; this phrase moves those end letters to the front

parts.note: to have wined is to have drunk wine

explanation.surface: A king drinks alongside a newspaper man who is sitting up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drank' gives WINED, which ends in ED, the usual crossword journalist; 'with journalist at the front' moves that ED to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin was a seventh-century King of Northumbria, and the name was borne by several Anglo-Saxon rulers.

clue.text: Edited stream about British YouTuber

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another
edited text is rewritten and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A cut-down livestream featuring a British video creator.
explanation.walkthrough: STREAM is rearranged around the B. MrBeast is an American creator with one of YouTube's biggest channels.
explanation.definitionFit: MrBeast, Jimmy Donaldson, is among the most-subscribed video creators on the platform.

clue.text: This makes music graduates tour Rhode Island

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so pieces surround another

parts.note: a Master of Arts
RI is the US state abbreviation

explanation.surface: Music graduates go on tour to Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music graduates' wants to be one phrase; music belongs to the definition, and graduates gives two degrees around RI.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a wooden-keyed percussion instrument, so it is a thing that produces music.

clue.text: The setter's sadly returned sausage

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the setter is I, and the setter's is I am
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: The compiler regrets that a sausage was sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter's' is read as I'm, not as a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, seasoned Italian sausage, often sliced thin.

clue.text: Urge all to suspect aggressive drinker

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, not to be trusted as it stands

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A call for everyone to treat a violent boozer as a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a verb in the surface; here it is an adjective marking the letters as unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: A lager lout is British slang for a young man who drinks heavily and becomes rowdy or violent.

clue.text: Statesman follows withdrawn musical instruction for players

indicators.note: following means coming after, so one piece goes second
something withdrawn is drawn back, so it runs backwards

parts.note: Cats, the Lloyd Webber musical
Cato, the Roman statesman

explanation.surface: A politician acts on a withdrawn musical direction meant for the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical instruction' wants to be one phrase; musical is the show, and the definition is only what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a score marking telling performers to play notes short and detached.

clue.text: Made the best of condition it imposed

indicators.note: to condition something is to alter its state, so its letters are remade

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone made the most of a condition that was forced on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condition' reads as a noun in the surface; it works as a verb meaning to modify.
explanation.definitionFit: To optimise is to make something as effective or favourable as possible, which is making the best of it.

clue.text: Cryptic indication of nocturnal mammals making attack sneakily

parts.note: the instruction word a setter would use

indicators.note: the answer is itself a clue-style instruction, telling the solver to turn something round

parts.note: bats are mammals that fly at night

explanation.surface: A cryptic-crossword clue about bats turns into an underhand assault.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a clue, the answer says 'back STAB', meaning reverse STAB to give BATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To backstab is to betray or attack someone treacherously while pretending friendship.

clue.text: What might contain your fare?

parts.note: surface reading: a purse or wallet holding the money for a bus or taxi; setter's reading: fare as food, specifically leftovers from a restaurant meal taken home in a container

explanation.walkthrough: Fare sounds like a ticket price, but it also means food; the container is for leftovers notionally meant for a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurants hand over a takeaway container for uneaten food, which holds the meal you ordered.

clue.text: Discontented, eighty revolutionary guards roughly dumping queen in capital

indicators.note: guards stand round what they protect, so one piece encloses another
a revolution turns things round, so the letters go backwards
without contents a word keeps only its outer shell

parts.note: outer letters of eighty

indicators.note: dumping means throwing away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: around means approximately
R for regina, queen

explanation.surface: Eighty disgruntled rebels mount guard, getting rid of the queen in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: YE wraps AROUND after its R is dropped. Yaoundé is the capital of Cameroon.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaoundé is Cameroon's seat of government, a national capital city in central Africa.

clue.text: Tibetan nearly crashes on your bike!

indicators.note: crashes suggests something smashed up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
nearly means the word is one letter short, losing its last

explanation.surface: A Tibetan cyclist almost has a crash and is told to get back on his bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' trims TIBETAN to TIBETA, and 'crashes' rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are brusque British phrases telling someone to go away, the first being slang for clear off.

clue.text: Food editor replaces front cover of authoritative works

indicators.note: the front cover of a word is its first letter, which is swapped out here

parts.note: a bible is any book treated as the authority on its subject

explanation.surface: An editor replaces the front cover of some definitive reference books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front cover' sounds like a book jacket, but it means the first letter, B, of BIBLES, which ED replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Edibles are things fit to be eaten, so the plural noun means food or provisions.

clue.text: Oaf loudly abandons puzzle

indicators.note: what abandons something leaves it, so that letter goes

parts.note: to flummox is to puzzle or baffle
F is forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A clumsy brute noisily gives up on a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: F, for forte, is removed from the verb meaning to baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lummox is a clumsy, stupid person, an informal synonym for a lout or oaf.

clue.text: Daisy's relative Iris perhaps discussed experiencing a blocked nose?

indicators.note: spoken with a cold, nasal consonants change, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: Iris Murdoch, the novelist, said with a heavy cold

explanation.surface: A daisy's kin, maybe an iris, talked about while sniffly.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris looks like a flower beside daisy; it is novelist Iris Murdoch, whose M turns to B with a blocked nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Burdock belongs to the daisy family, Asteraceae, so it is a botanical relative.

clue.text: Barman will regularly fight

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: The bartender often gets into a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' reads as often in the surface; it picks alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rough, noisy scuffle, so it is a kind of fight.

clue.text: Peacekeepers provided soldiers with male clothing

parts.note: United Nations peacekeeping forces
provided means on condition that, if
other ranks, ordinary soldiers
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers issued troops with men's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the crossword staple for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniform is the standard outfit worn by members of a group, so it is clothing.

clue.text: Many Times newspaper cuts upset one

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the newspaper goes inside the other letters
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of one are rearranged

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's job cuts upset one of its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many Times' is the definition, not the newspaper; the paper is FT, which 'cuts' into OEN, the letters of 'one' 'upset'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something many times is doing it frequently, which is what the adverb means.

clue.text: Seed of a scam inspiring hacker, ultimately

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so one piece is drawn inside

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter

parts.note: last letter of hacker

explanation.surface: The seed of a fraud that eventually motivated a computer hacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seed of a scam' reads as the origin of a fraud; Seed is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak, which contains the tree's seed.

clue.text: Models work transiently and steal desperately

parts.note: to temp is to do temporary office work

indicators.note: acting desperately is acting wildly, so the letters go out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fashion models taking short-term jobs turn to desperate theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Models' wants to be catwalk people; here it means patterns to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or guide used as a model for making copies.

clue.text: Post-holder improved security for Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: improved means made better
locks provide security, and the word is said aloud as lox

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better locks' with its first sounds swapped is spoken as letter box.
explanation.definitionFit: A letterbox is a slot or box that receives mail, so it holds the post.

clue.text: Regressive parties controlling US city council

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the letters run in reverse
to control is to hold, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: do is slang for a party, plural dos
New York

explanation.walkthrough: 'Regressive parties' reads as political parties; parties are dos, celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church clergy, an ecclesiastical council.
